replies.reply:
OPTIONS:
- Creep up beside Hester and peek through the keyhole gap myself, to see the jar of shadows with my own eyes (for: learning what is inside and how to free the shadows before midnight)
- Stay in the grass with Dilly and keep watch for the peddler while Hester peeks (for: not getting caught and keeping our retreat open)
- Whisper to Dilly to hold her lamp low and ready, and ask her to stand guard at the wagon steps while Hester and I look inside (for: giving us light and a lookout together)
* Whisper to Dilly to keep her lamp low and watch the lane, then creep to Hester's side and ask what she sees (for: getting news of the jar quickly while someone still guards our backs)
DO: I put a finger to my lips and whisper to Dilly, "Goodness, you're loud as a dropped button box! Keep that lamp low and watch the lane for the peddler." Then I creep through the grass to Hester's side and murmur, "Well, colleague, what do you see? Is the jar there?"
JOURNAL: Dilly has arrived, so my back is guarded and I can go closer without leaving us blind. Hester promised me the first word about the jar, and I want to know how to get the shadows out before midnight, and to be the one who did it.

OPTIONS:
- Creep up beside Hester and peek through the keyhole gap myself, so I see the jar with my own eyes (for: learning what's in the wagon before anyone goes in)
- Stay crouched with Dilly and whisper a plan: Dilly keeps the lamp low and watches the lane while Hester and I look inside (for: not being caught by the peddler)
- Go straight up the steps and in through the open door while the peddler is out (for: reaching the jar of shadows before midnight)
* Wave Dilly down into the grass, whisper to her to keep the lamp low and watch the lane, then creep up beside Hester to look through the gap (for: a lookout behind us and a look at the jar before we risk going in)
DO: I hiss, "Goodness, Dilly, down, down, and tuck that lamp low! Watch the lane for the peddler and give a whistle if he comes." Then I gather my shawl and creep through the grass to Hester's side, whispering, "Well? Is the jar there? Let me have a look too."
JOURNAL: Dilly arriving means we have a lookout at last, so I can safely join Hester rather than sit idle. I want to see that jar before anyone steps in, because the children's shadows are the way to wake them before midnight, and I'd love to be the one who gets them back.

OPTIONS:
- Ask Mister Tibbersnatch what the whistle is for and why he wants one that's well loved (for: finding out whether he's still a danger before I bargain with him)
- Head up to the Tock Tower and look at the old tin whistle myself (for: seeing what the whistle is and whether it's worth anything before anyone trades it)
- Go back up to Crooked Lane and the square to tell everyone who showed the way (for: getting my name said alongside the fix)
* Keep Tibbersnatch talking and haggle over the jar, asking plainly what the whistle is for and what he'd give for it (for: learning his game and getting a bargain out of it)
DO: "Whistle, chum? Now there's a price I'd want to hear the whole of before I say a word. Easy as winking, I'll fetch you one, but what's it for, and what's it worth to you? Something better than rhymes, I hope, because a lamplighter doesn't work for rhymes." I keep my pole planted and my eye on his long fingers.
JOURNAL: The shadows are home, but he's still smiling too wide and asking for a whistle, and I can't walk past a bargain without learning the price. I want to know what he's really after before I go fetching anything, and if there's a fix to be made out of it, I want to be the one who made it.

OPTIONS:
- Ask Mister Tibbersnatch what a worn-in whistle is to him and why he wants it, since he named his price (for: finding out whether trading with him is a bargain or a trap)
- Head back up Crooked Lane to the Lopsided Square and tell Pip and Mags the shadows are home, so the town knows who was in the wagon (for: getting my name said alongside the fix)
- Climb to the Tock Tower to look at the old tin whistle everyone says is up there (for: seeing what it is worth before anyone hands it to a peddler)
* Press Tibbersnatch on what the whistle is for and what he'd give for it, before I think about fetching anything (for: learning the price before I commit, and keeping him from slipping away unquestioned)
DO: "A whistle, is it, chum? Easy as winking, I can't pass a bargain, but I ask the cost before I ask the thing. Why that whistle, and what would you give me for it? Name it plain, no rhymes, and I'll tell you whether Dilly Quickstep's interested."
JOURNAL: The shadows are home, but the peddler is still grinning in the meadow and wants a whistle from the Tock Tower, and I'd rather know what he's really after before I run off fetching it. If there's a bargain in it, I want to be the one who struck it, and the one the town remembers.

OPTIONS:
- Knock again at another window, or push the broken garden gate open and look for a lit window inside (for: finding a child who has woken, since this stretch of wall has no window)
- Go on north up Crooked Lane to the Lopsided Square, where the shadows are heading and the lit windows are (for: seeing a child wake with my own goggles before anyone fetches the whistle)
- Go back to the meadow and press Tibbersnatch on his bargain (for: settling the whistle question)
* Go north to the Lopsided Square with Marigold, following the shadows (for: seeing a child wake with my own goggles before anyone fetches the whistle)
DO: "Marigold, my dear colleague, this wall has no window and I've been courting masonry. Hypothesis: the shadows know the way home better than we do. Test: follow them!" I tuck the poker under my arm and stride north up the lane after the small pelting shadows, beckoning Marigold along, keeping an eye out for any lit window with a child in it.
JOURNAL: My knock went to a wall, so there's no sense lingering, and the shadows are all running to the square where the lit windows are. I won't call the experiment a success until I see a child's eyes open, and only then will we look hard at that whistle and decide what to do about Tibbersnatch's bargain.

OPTIONS:
- Knock again at another house, or push through the open garden gate on its one hinge, to find a window with a child behind it (for: seeing a child wake with my own goggles)
- Go back down to the meadow and press Tibbersnatch about the whistle (for: settling the bargain and getting the jar)
* Follow the pelting shadows north up to the Lopsided Square, where the lit windows are, with Marigold (for: finding a window that actually answers and seeing a child wake)
- Stay and scribble in my notebook about the stove that ticks in time with the clock (for: understanding how the trick was done)
DO: "Marigold, my dear colleague, this wall is deaf as a turnip! Hypothesis: the shadows know the way home better than we do. Test: follow them." I tuck the poker under my arm and stride north up the lane after the little tumbling shadows, calling back, "Up to the square, where the lit windows are, and keep your ears open for the clock!"
JOURNAL: The wall gave me nothing, but the shadows are all heading for the square, and that is where the lit windows are, so I'll let them lead. I won't call the experiment a success until I've seen a child open their eyes, and only then will I think about the whistle and that grinning peddler.
